pr_body:
Fixes #70199.

<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.
PRs can target `3.x` if the same change was done in `master`, or is not relevant there.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.
You can mention in the description if the change is compatible with `3.x`.
-->
pr_comments: `#else` in [line 249](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/fd4f882bd9b9fedefdacedfbf813aefa65d2568c#diff-a3dac44e3d02774569e24f3cac9d6e3842fe626380e022f9d0090a503058828dR249) could be replaced by `#endif` because of `return` statement I think
Note that these might be issues @Riteo already handled in the Wayland work (didn't check).

@akien-mga yup, I already handled them in my PR, thanks for letting me know!

IIRC I didn't make a PR because I though that this would technically only concern Wayland, but it looks like I was wrong. Why is this needed here though?

Edit: damn ctrl+enter again! Added the rest.

Edit2: Here is the diff btw (note that this depends on Wayland):
```diff
diff --git a/modules/openxr/SCsub b/modules/openxr/SCsub
index 84542be3b9..aa2dbf72fd 100644
--- a/modules/openxr/SCsub
+++ b/modules/openxr/SCsub
@@ -33,6 +33,9 @@ elif env["platform"] == "linuxbsd":
     if env["x11"]:
         env_openxr.AppendUnique(CPPDEFINES=["XR_USE_PLATFORM_XLIB"])
 
+    if env["wayland"]:
+        env_openxr.AppendUnique(CPPDEFINES=["XR_USE_PLATFORM_WAYLAND"])
+
     # FIXME: Review what needs to be set for Android and macOS.
     env_openxr.AppendUnique(CPPDEFINES=["HAVE_SECURE_GETENV"])
 elif env["platform"] == "windows":
@@ -90,7 +93,8 @@ if env["platform"] == "android":
     env_openxr.add_source_files(module_obj, "extensions/openxr_android_extension.cpp")
 if env["vulkan"]:
     env_openxr.add_source_files(module_obj, "extensions/openxr_vulkan_extension.cpp")
-if env["opengl3"]:
+if env["opengl3"] and (env["platform"] != "linuxbsd" or env["x11"]):
+    # On Linux/BSD, the OpenGL extension should only be enabled when at least X11 is enabled.
     env_openxr.add_source_files(module_obj, "extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp")
 
 env_openxr.add_source_files(module_obj, "extensions/openxr_palm_pose_extension.cpp")
diff --git a/modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp b/modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp
index 3b7c130149..5df6e176aa 100644
--- a/modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp
+++ b/modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp
@@ -126,6 +126,10 @@ void *OpenXROpenGLExtension::set_session_create_and_get_next_pointer(void *p_nex
 
 	DisplayServer *display_server = DisplayServer::get_singleton();
 
+#ifdef WAYLAND_ENABLED
+	ERR_FAIL_COND_V_MSG(display_server->get_name() == "Wayland", p_next_pointer, "OpenXR is not yet supported on OpenGL Wayland.");
+#endif
+
 #ifdef WIN32
 	graphics_binding_gl.type = XR_TYPE_GRAPHICS_BINDING_OPENGL_WIN32_KHR,
 	graphics_binding_gl.next = p_next_pointer;
```

Removing some Wayland references, I think that this should be what you're looking for, from looking at the diff (although it's been a while since I made these changes and might've forgot some important detail, be aware)

Edit3: All right, this stuff doesn't stop Godot from registering the OpenGL API, nor does it guard the include. Not sure what happened here tbh. Perhaps some change after I made that PR? Anyways, that logic will have to be added separately.

Hi @Riteo , thanks for the diff! Is the PR that you're working on going to incorporate this change as well, or should I try to duplicate your code and make it work with X11 as well? (note: the problem here is that, when building with `x11=no`, some classes should be excluded from the final build, and currently they are not, so we get some errors).

@Riteo wrote:

> IIRC I didn't make a PR because I though that this would technically only concern Wayland, but it looks like I was wrong. Why is this needed here though?

I'm also a little unclear about why we're implementing the ability to build without X11, when we don't have any alternative (like Wayland) available yet.

Also, thinking about this a little more, if X11 is disabled, shouldn't that imply that OpenGL is disabled too? Since we're using GLX, we can't initialize OpenGL without initializing X11. Maybe the build system should automatically set `opengl3=no` on Linux if `x11=no` is set? (Of course, once we have Wayland support, this won't be right anymore :-))

> I'm also a little unclear about why we're implementing the ability to build without X11, when we don't have any alternative (like Wayland) available yet.

for server/headless builds running godot from command line
Thanks for all the hints, I'll try to come up with a solution soon ;)

@Riteo @dsnopek I've changed the code a bit and now Linux + no X11 results in `extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp` not being included at all. Also, Linux + no X11 automatically removes `GLES3_ENABLED`, which I hope will result in all relevant parts of the code being removed from the build.

There is still a new `#ifndef` in `platform/linuxbsd/os_linuxbsd.cpp`, but that file looks rather generic, so I don't think I can remove it all based on `GLES3_ENABLED` ;) This small change will only influence `get_video_adapter_driver_info`. Let me know if it's OK :)

I think I might also remove the extra check in this condition:
```
if env["opengl3"] and (env["platform"] or env["x11"]):
    env_openxr.add_source_files(module_obj, "extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp")
```
because `GLES3_ENABLED` should cover that file as well. I'll check later if the build works.
BTW, should there be a new GitHub action to check `x11=no` builds?

Thanks for working on this!

You all did good research, but neither of the two fixes remaining in this PR after discussion seem correct :P
They work, but they're overkill.

I opened #73504 to fix the build with the IMO correct changes (could be refined further for OpenXR to only disable the extension which requires `XrGraphicsBindingOpenGLXlibKHR` if someone is interested).

issue_context.title: Cannot compile Godot without x server - `scons x11=no`
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Godot beta 8

### System information

Ubuntu 22.10 - AMD RX 470, Gnome shell 43 X11

### Issue description

```
scons x11=no
```
show this error
```
platform/linuxbsd/os_linuxbsd.cpp: In member function 'virtual Vector<String> OS_LinuxBSD::get_video_adapter_driver_info() const':
platform/linuxbsd/os_linuxbsd.cpp:247:13: error: 'RenderingServer' has not been declared
  247 |         if (RenderingServer::get_singleton()->get_rendering_device() == nullptr) {
      |             ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
platform/linuxbsd/os_linuxbsd.cpp:251:46: error: 'RenderingServer' has not been declared
  251 |         const String rendering_device_name = RenderingServer::get_singleton()->get_rendering_device()->get_device_name(); // e.g. `NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970`
      |                                              ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
platform/linuxbsd/os_linuxbsd.cpp:252:48: error: 'RenderingServer' has not been declared
  252 |         const String rendering_device_vendor = RenderingServer::get_singleton()->get_rendering_device()->get_device_vendor_name(); // e.g. `NVIDIA`
      |                                                ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

```

### Steps to reproduce

Above

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
I'd like to submit a fix. I'm not sure what should `OS_LinuxBSD::get_video_adapter_driver_info()` return when X11 is disabled, so I've set it to an empty Vector. If it should be a specific value, please let me know, I'll update the code.

I think that if X11 is disabled, GLES3 should also be disabled automatically. I'll check if it's possible to set it, since it would simplify my PR and would probably be the proper way of handling this situation (instead of adding double ifs everywhere). What do you think?

      |                                              ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
platform/linuxbsd/os_linuxbsd.cpp:255:48: error: 'RenderingServer' has not been declared

Which is the original error mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70199 .

@pfertyk bruh, this makes _some_ sense but I'd have expected it to have some sort of mock server. Anyways, while I'd keep an eye on these things as stuff goes on, I'll mark this conversation as resolved as this looks like the best option rn.

Edit: always forget that conversation resolving is extremely locked, you'll have to do it yourself :moyai:
I don't know why RenderingServer isn't defined without x11 though, it should be working with the headless mode?
@akien-mga thought the same thing, but I think that this might be material for another PR.
For headless builds I currently use this patch: https://github.com/LinuxUserGD/gdscript-transpiler-bin/blob/dev/.github/workflows/headless-build.patch
@LinuxUserGD I think that's the same thing.

Current solution in this PR is consistent with a check earlier in this file:
```
#ifdef X11_ENABLED
#include "x11/display_server_x11.h"
#endif
```

So, if X11 is not define, we don't include the symbols.

Should I try to create a mockup for RenderingServer if X11 is off, or (as @Riteo mentioned) this should be done in a different PR?
@pfertyk for some reason I noticed this message only now. I think that this is material for a separate PR.
OK, thanks for feedback ;) Is there anything else I should update in this PR?
@pfertyk if it works fine no. It does indeed look fine.
